svg.title: Expanse on WebAssembly: exact fuel per operation on wasm32 (32-bit engine) and wasm64 (64-bit engine), and bytes per key
svg.text: Expanse on WebAssembly — one source, two engines, exact fuel
wasm32 selects the 32-bit engine and wasm64 the 64-bit engine; each row is one fixture on both, under one runtime. Fuel is the Callgrind analogue for the wasm targets and gates every wasm PR.
fuel units per operation, exact; shorter is better; label is wasm64 ÷ wasm32
fuel units per operation, exact; shorter is better; label is wasm64 ÷ wasm32
bytes per key, the engine's own mem_used
N = 10,000 after the build; exact; label wasm64 ÷ wasm32
the 64-bit engine consumes less fuel on 29 of 30 arms; the 32-bit engine holds a map key in 52–54% of the bytes
fuel counts executed wasm instructions under wasmtime: not cycles, not wall clock, and not a mechanism — why one engine spends fewer is not measured (AGENTS.md §8.9)
measured: Darwin arm64, wasmtime 48.0.0 (Python bindings, fuel metering, two fresh-instance runs agreeing to the unit)
wasm32 built by rustc 1.98.0 (88d9e12ae 2026-08-18); wasm64 built by rustc 1.100.0-nightly (2e2b193f8 2026-09-02) with -Z build-std
commit 55d4de06; module crates/expanse-wasm-fuel, driver scripts/wasm_fuel.py; source results/baseline_wasm_fuel.json (N = 10,000); the same source builds both targets
